IBM: RAMAC 'was the size of two kitchen refrigerators, weighed more than a ton'

post.instagram_caption:
The first commercial hard drive weighed more than a ton.

IBM's Model 350 shipped in 1956. It stacked fifty 24-inch disks in a cabinet IBM compares to two kitchen refrigerators, and it held the equivalent of about 3.75 megabytes. Companies leased it for $750 a month (Computer History Museum).

Today, one terabyte equals about 267,000 of them.

The lesson: storage got cheap, so now we keep everything.

Source: Computer History Museum and IBM, checked Nov 20, 2026.

post.youtube_description:
IBM's Model 350, the first commercial hard disk drive, shipped in 1956. It used fifty 24-inch disks, was about the size of two kitchen refrigerators, weighed more than a ton and stored the equivalent of about 3.75 megabytes. Companies leased it for $750 a month. One terabyte today equals about 267,000 of them.
